headline: cuVSLAM + Gaussian Splatting · city-scale under 5GB VRAM · 34ms → 19ms jitter
achievements: Built an end-to-end ROS 2 mapping and navigation pipeline: RealSense D435i feeding NVIDIA Isaac ROS cuVSLAM 3.2 for real-time visual-inertial SLAM, with a synchronized 2Hz capture node
Audited the RealSense driver end to end, found 11 distinct misconfigurations degrading SLAM tracking, and tightened jitter tolerance from 34ms to 19ms
Migrated an abandoned robot simulation across a discontinued Isaac Sim release, fixing nine categories of breaking changes including a full Python API namespace migration

Diagnosed a silent multi-camera sensor-fusion failure by proving two cameras sixty degrees apart couldn't triangulate depth, redesigned the camera rig, and built a tool to derive LiDAR intrinsics directly from live data
Built a custom Gaussian Splatting pipeline from scratch for high-fidelity 3D scene reconstruction, and developed feed-forward methods that work from minimal input views

Designed a 3-machine distributed ROS 2 system over a Tailscale mesh, choosing a FastDDS Discovery Server over CycloneDDS since multicast doesn't traverse VPN tunnels, then tracked down a Tailscale tun0 userspace-networking bug via FastDDS interface whitelisting
Wrote a three-way coordinate-frame translation layer across ROS, OpenGL, and COLMAP conventions, plus a quaternion-SLERP correction scheme so loop-closure pose jumps stay geometrically consistent
Researched city-scale Gaussian Splatting with memory-efficient scene representations, running on a single GPU under 5GB VRAM — not a multi-GPU cluster
Fused CLIP and DINOv2 features into the splat representation, so a reconstructed environment can be queried and localized in natural language

Architected a full sim-in-the-loop autonomy stack on Isaac Sim, chaining visual-inertial SLAM, 3D reconstruction, navigation, and autonomous exploration into one GPU-accelerated pipeline for a ground robot
Enabled zero-copy GPU image transport between perception and navigation stages, and cut the LiDAR's data volume four-fold after finding it starved the navigation stack
Authored a custom multi-sensor payload in URDF/xacro (dual RGB-D + 3D spinning LiDAR) with matching Isaac Sim sensor publishers, keeping every simulated topic consistent with the real driver's layout

Decoupled the simulator's physics tick rate from its render rate, running physics at 180Hz against 60Hz rendering, after measuring that render-rate updates left the inertial data too sparse for reliable SLAM tracking
Implemented multiple research papers into end-to-end pipelines for 3D reconstruction techniques
description: Built a ROS 2 pipeline that starts at a RealSense feed and ends at a language-queryable 3D scene: cuVSLAM for real-time visual-inertial tracking, a custom Gaussian Splatting reconstruction stack, and CLIP/DINOv2 features fused into the splats. Most of the work has been the audit trail — RealSense misconfigurations, sensor-fusion failures, Isaac Sim breaking changes — that has to get fixed before any of that runs reliably.

headline: 30% faster 3D reconstruction · 40% faster failure response
achievements: Deployed the Gaussian Splatting reconstruction pipeline on Kubernetes with dynamic GPU allocation across H100, A100, and T4 tiers, cutting processing time 30%

Built a physics-estimation pipeline that infers Young's modulus, Poisson's ratio, density, and friction for reconstructed deformable and rigid objects from visual features and texture, connecting 3D reconstruction to physical-world understanding

Managed Kubernetes cluster state and infrastructure provisioning with Terraform, and set up the deployment workflow end to end on ArgoCD, giving the team a GitOps-driven path from a config change to a running cluster
Built the monitoring and alerting layer on Prometheus and Grafana so failures surfaced instead of hiding in logs, cutting failure response time 40%
Designed and deployed a scalable asynchronous job scheduling platform on Argo Workflows, improving pipeline stability and reliability
description: Connected physics to pixels: built a pipeline that infers material properties from reconstructed 3D geometry, then deployed it alongside the existing Gaussian Splatting stack on Kubernetes with GPU-tier-aware scheduling and real monitoring.

headline: 50% faster inference · 60% cost reduction · <500ms latency
achievements: Built detection, segmentation, and classification models (ViT, Faster-RCNN, Mask-RCNN, YOLO) with custom loss and activation functions, gaining up to 20% accuracy
Designed a serverless inference platform on Kubernetes using Triton Inference Server, KServe, KNative, and gRPC, serving multiple models under 500ms latency
Improved inference performance 50% and cut infrastructure costs 60% through multithreading, vectorization, and FP16/INT8 precision on A100 and T4 GPUs
Deployed vision models to Jetson and Raspberry Pi boards under hard latency budgets using quantization, pruning, and distillation: 40% faster inference, 20% smaller models
Built a model-caching algorithm that cut scale-up time from 15-20 minutes to 3-4 seconds

Built streaming and bidirectional gRPC servers on top of Triton, plus custom extension interfaces for specialized inference workloads, connecting Android and JavaScript clients via gRPC, ConnectRPC, and REST — including Kotlin gRPC clients for the Android integration
Led and mentored a team of 6+ engineers, and secured roughly $200K in NVIDIA and Azure cloud-credit partnerships

Presented technical updates and new AI approaches directly to investors, company directors, and other non-technical stakeholders, translating what a model could and couldn't do into decisions the wider team could act on
description: Led CV team at an agriculture AI startup — custom model architectures, edge deployment on Jetson, distributed inference on Kubernetes. Five years of production constraints will teach you more about robustness than any textbook. Eventually decided to go formalize what was working with a proper robotics degree.

headline: Led 5 engineers · Best Team Award · in-house serverless inference platform
achievements: Selected into TCS Rapid Labs, an internal AI and robotics R&D cohort running fast three-month proof-of-concept cycles
Led a team of 5 engineers building full-stack proof-of-concepts, architecting the cloud and HPC infrastructure behind them
Spearheaded an in-house serverless inference and deployment platform for computer vision, NLP, and multi-modal models
Built a data-cleaning algorithm to detect and remove duplicate repeated data from PDFs, gaining 20% efficiency
Shipped multiple NLP proof-of-concepts using BERT and Transformer models
Won the Best Team Award for the cohort
description: Built NLP and full-stack proof-of-concepts inside TCS Rapid Labs, an internal three-month-cycle R&D cohort, and led the 5-engineer team that won the cohort's Best Team Award.
